short.title: The Writing on the Wall
short.blurb: A king throws a lavish feast and drinks from stolen temple gold. Then the fingers of a human hand appear and write on the palace wall.

story.title: David and Goliath
story.blurb: A giant soldier taunts a terrified army for forty days, until a shepherd boy delivering bread to his brothers asks why nobody has answered him.

short.title: We're All Mad Here
short.blurb: Lost at a crossroads, a girl asks a grinning cat for directions and receives logic, a diagnosis of madness, and an invitation to croquet.

story.title: A Mad Tea Party
story.blurb: A girl sits down uninvited at an endless tea table, where the riddles have no answers, the watch runs on butter, and it is always six o'clock.

short.title: There's Glory for You
short.blurb: Humpty Dumpty quizzes a polite girl on birthdays and arithmetic, then announces that a word means exactly what he chooses it to mean.

story.title: Tweedledum and Tweedledee
story.blurb: Two round brothers agree to battle over a spoiled new rattle, armoured in bolsters and coal scuttles, while something dark flies toward the wood.

short.title: A Dog for a Nurse
short.blurb: A tidy London family cannot afford a proper nurse, so they engage a Newfoundland dog named Nana, who takes childcare very seriously indeed.

story.title: The Boy Who Lost His Shadow
story.blurb: A crying boy breaks into a nursery hunting for his lost shadow, and the girl who wakes knows exactly what to do about it.

short.title: Evil, Be Thou My Good
short.blurb: A ruined spirit, utterly alone, asks whether any way back remains, and talks himself out of every answer but one.

short.title: The Thief and the Innkeeper
short.blurb: A guest who cannot pay his bill yawns, howls like a wolf, and politely asks the innkeeper to hold his clothes.

short.title: The Ships in the Bay
short.blurb: From a high bank above the Chesapeake, an enslaved boy watches white sails glide out to freedom and pours his whole heart after them.

story.title: The Battle with Covey
story.blurb: Carrying a root said to protect him from any whipping, an enslaved young man decides one Monday morning that he will fight back.

short.title: No Place for Repentance
short.blurb: Alone with himself, a fallen spirit weighs pardon against pride, counts what surrender would cost him, and makes his choice.

story.title: The Gates of Hell
story.blurb: A fleeing rebel spirit reaches ninefold gates of brass, iron, and rock, and finds two monstrous shapes guarding them, one wearing the likeness of a crown.
story.spoilerNote: Hints that the shapes guarding the gate are Satan's own kin, a disclosure the poem stages as a revelation just after this scene.
story.brokenNote: The passage opens and closes mid-sentence, cutting off Satan's reply before the standoff resolves.

short.title: No Trickery
short.blurb: After dinner, an inventor asks his sceptical guests to examine a beautifully made little machine, then invites one of them to press the lever.

story.title: The White Sphinx
story.blurb: A reckless traveller hurls himself into futurity, then risks everything to stop. He lands in hail and blossoms under the gaze of a marble sphinx.

short.title: The Thing in the Pit
short.blurb: A crowd gathers at a pit expecting a man to climb out of the fallen cylinder. What emerges instead glistens like wet leather.
short.spoilerNote: Shows what the invaders actually look like, a horror the book builds up to across its opening chapters.

story.title: The Third Falling Star
story.blurb: Driving home near midnight under a gathering storm, a man sees a green thread of fire fall into a field, and then something enormous begins to walk.
story.spoilerNote: Reveals the invaders' giant walking machines, whose first appearance the book stages as a shock.

story.title: The Story of the Door
story.blurb: Out on a walk, a gentleman points to a shabby door and tells of a trampled child, a hateful stranger, and a cheque signed with an unmentionable name.

43.pairNote: These two do not overlap each other, but the short duplicates a stretch inside book 42's story span, since 42 and 43 are editions of the same novel.

short.title: The Juggernaut
short.blurb: Three in the morning, streets empty and lamplit, a lone walker longing for the sight of a policeman. Then two figures collide at a corner.

story.title: Mr. Seek
story.blurb: A lawyer keeps watch on a shabby door by every light and hour, determined to see the face of a man he has never met.

short.title: Call Me Cordelia
short.blurb: Asked her name, a small orphan opens negotiations instead: she pleads for an elegant alias, and failing that, for one crucial letter.

story.title: The Raspberry Cordial
story.blurb: Keeping house for the first time, a talkative girl pours her best friend generous tumblerfuls of raspberry cordial and chatters on, not noticing anything amiss.

short.title: More Gravy Than Grave
short.blurb: A bitter old man tells the ghost sitting opposite that he does not believe in it, and blames his supper. The spectre listens, perfectly motionless.

story.title: Fezziwig's Ball
story.blurb: A spirit leads an old man back to the warehouse where he was apprenticed, just as the shutters go up and a Christmas Eve ball begins.

short.title: The Cowardly Lion
short.blurb: A great lion springs at a little dog and gets its nose slapped by a furious little girl. The conversation that follows surprises everyone.

story.title: The Witch's Silver Whistle
story.blurb: From her castle door, a witch whose single eye sees everywhere spies four travelers crossing her country. She blows her silver whistle, and wolves come running first.

short.title: Winning the Watchdog
short.blurb: A stranger on a strange world sits down beside his fearsome guard beast, puts his arms around its neck, and coaxes it like a hound from home.

short.title: The Red Star Answers
short.blurb: For ten years a man has prayed beneath a red star, arms outstretched, begging to be carried back across the void. Tonight something answers.

story.title: Before the Gates of Kaol
story.blurb: Waked at dawn by stealthy movement, a lone swordsman spies a silent line of green warriors hidden beside the road, waiting to slaughter a city's unsuspecting troops.

short.title: Mistress of the Man-Eaters
short.blurb: Great predators look up from their feast and pad toward two travelers. The man draws his sword; the girl tells him to put it away.

story.title: Insult in the Royal Garden
story.blurb: In a royal garden, a prince presses unwanted love on a princess and seizes her arm. Her cry brings the guard, and someone far swifter.

short.title: The Forest Chapel
short.blurb: Deep in the forest, arching boughs make a quiet chapel floored with pine needles. A young soldier pushes the green doors aside and steps in.

story.title: The Tattered Man
story.blurb: A road streams with wounded men, cursing, singing, staggering to the rear. A boy falls in with the march, and a stranger with a gentle voice keeps pace beside him.
story.spoilerNote: Reveals the young soldier has no wound of his own, hinting he ran from the battle.

74.pairNote: Two separate pranks from different days; neither borrows the other's payoff.

short.title: The Cat and the Painkiller
short.blurb: A boy offers his aunt's cat a taste of patent medicine, and the cat accepts. What follows involves flower pots, somersaults, and an open window.

story.title: The Glorious Whitewasher
story.blurb: Sentenced to whitewash thirty yards of fence on a perfect Saturday, a boy discovers a law of human nature that turns his punishment into a privilege.

76.pairNote: A quiet night scene and a steamboat escapade, with no shared text or shared payoff.

short.title: The Signal at Midnight
short.blurb: Alone at midnight, a superstitious boy reads doom in a shriveled spider, until a soft meow from the dark trees tells him adventure is waiting.

story.title: Trapped on the Wreck
story.blurb: Creeping through a wrecked steamboat in the dark, a boy overhears two men deciding how a third will die, then finds his own escape has floated away.

84.pairNote: The creation night and the glacier meeting are distinct scenes; each lands on its own.

short.title: A Dreary Night of November
short.blurb: On a rainy November night, after two years of secret labor, a young scientist watches a dull yellow eye open, and his dream curdles into horror.

story.title: Creature and Creator
story.blurb: High on a glacier, a maker meets the being he made and abandoned. The creature asks only to be heard, and his plea is harder to refuse than to hate.
story.spoilerNote: Reveals that the creature has already murdered the narrator's young brother, a death the book stages as a shock.

story.title: The Eclipse
story.blurb: Chained to the stake before four thousand silent watchers, a condemned man bets his life on the sky going dark at exactly the right moment.
story.spoilerNote: Gives away how the hero escapes execution, the payoff of the book's opening predicament.

story.title: One Hundred and Five, North Tower
story.blurb: A wine merchant turns cannonier as a living sea of people breaks against a fortress. When the towers fall, he wants one cell above all.
story.brokenNote: The text stops in the middle of a sentence while describing the cell, so the story ends mid air.

short.title: Four Minutes Too Slow
short.blurb: A young Frenchman of many trades applies to serve the most exact gentleman in England, and learns his new master counts life in minutes.

short.title: The Obvious Facts
short.blurb: A wild eyed young man bursts in on two friends at breakfast, certain his name explains everything. His host knows only what a glance can tell, which is plenty.

short.title: The Animal Charmer
short.blurb: In a spring wood a girl finds a boy playing a wooden pipe while a squirrel, a pheasant, and two rabbits creep close to listen.

120.pairNote: Two different visitors menace the same inn guest, but each confrontation has its own arc and payoff.

short.title: A Battle of Looks
short.blurb: In a quiet parlour, a drunken old seaman draws a knife on the one guest who refuses to be afraid of him.

story.title: Black Dog Appears and Disappears
story.blurb: A pale stranger missing two fingers waits behind an inn door for his old shipmate Bill, and the reunion ends in drawn cutlasses.

121.pairNote: Two separate flirtations built on the same teasing wit, with no shared text and separate punch lines.

short.title: The Duties of a Partner
short.blurb: At a ball, a young lady's new partner performs both halves of polite small talk, smirks included, and she can barely keep from laughing.

story.title: Nerves Fit for Sliding Panels
story.blurb: Riding toward an old abbey, a young reader of horrid novels hears her companion describe, in loving detail, the gloomy chamber and hidden manuscript awaiting her.

135.pairNote: Two unrelated scenes, a child in the forest and a stranger at a fireside; nothing shared.

short.title: The Night Errand
short.blurb: Sent for water after dark, a small girl stands frozen between the terrors of the night forest and the woman waiting at home.

story.title: The Convict at the Door
story.blurb: Turned away from every inn and even a dog's kennel, a weary stranger announces exactly what he is at a quiet fireside, and waits to be cast out.

139.pairNote: The short is the scene immediately before the story begins; no shared text, and each lands its own joke.

short.title: Fair Warning
short.blurb: Before a young visitor meets the notorious professor, the great man's wife takes him aside with urgent instructions on surviving the encounter.

story.title: An Audience with the Professor
story.blurb: A journalist bluffs his way into a volcanic scientist's study armed with borrowed jargon, hoping the great man will not notice.

story.title: The Two Wills
story.blurb: At three in the morning a dying miser, all his faculties sharp, orders his young night-nurse to open the iron chest and burn one of his two wills.
story.spoilerNote: Gives away the two-wills deathbed night behind the book's inheritance surprise, though not which will stands.

short.title: Forty Yards of Lion
short.blurb: Alone on foot with a rifle, a traveller faces his first charging lion and coolly reasons where the single stopping bullet must go.

155.pairNote: A battlefield prologue and a quiet seaside scene told by a different narrator; nothing shared.

short.title: The Curse in the Armoury
short.blurb: Amid the sack of a palace, an officer follows screams to a torchlit room, a bloodied dagger, and a dying man's last words.

story.title: The Shivering Sand
story.blurb: An old house-steward tries to coax a sad young housemaid away from the quicksand that draws her, until an unexpected arrival changes her face.

158.pairNote: A domestic comic miniature and a drawing-room persuasion scene; different characters at the centre, nothing shared.

short.title: The Matter of the Wedding-Cake
short.blurb: A kindly invalid who distrusts all rich food wages a polite one-man campaign against the neighbourhood's wedding-cake.

story.title: I Would Not Influence You
story.blurb: A farmer's heartfelt proposal arrives by letter, and a young woman's clever friend insists, repeatedly, that the decision must be entirely her own.

160.pairNote: Two scenes from the same summer night, the swim and then the hammock; sequential with no shared text, and each carries its own charge.

short.title: First Swim by Moonlight
short.blurb: After a summer of failed lessons, a woman suddenly finds her stroke one night and swims out alone toward the moonlit horizon.

story.title: The Hammock
story.blurb: Past midnight, a wife stays out in the hammock; her husband commands, coaxes, and finally sits smoking beside a will he cannot move.

short.title: The Gentleman in the Rain
short.blurb: A twisted ankle on a wet hillside brings a handsome stranger who carries the injured girl home and leaves the whole household wondering.

story.title: The Pearl Diver and the Shark
story.blurb: From the shadow of a rock, undersea watchers observe a poor diver work his oyster bed, until a huge shape glides over him.

short.title: The Doctor's Menagerie
short.blurb: In a dim vault, a captor fondles his marmoset and lovingly catalogues the scorpions, pythons, and spiders he keeps for his enemies.

short.title: Talking Through Wagner
short.blurb: An unexpected caller sweeps in, dressed as if by a tempest, and explains why she loves loud opera: one can talk the whole time without being heard.

story.title: The Girl in the Greenroom
story.blurb: Fresh from a disastrous performance, an actress glows with secret joy, certain her lover will understand why she can no longer pretend on stage.
story.spoilerNote: Reveals that Dorian turns on the actress Sibyl and destroys their engagement, an early turning point in the novel.

story.title: The Voice in Box Five
story.blurb: At the peak of her triumph, a soprano opens her mouth and an impossible sound comes out, while two managers feel an unseen presence breathing beside them.
story.spoilerNote: Gives away the ghost's sabotage of Carlotta and the chandelier disaster, a famous set piece the novel stages as a shock.

story.title: The Fight with Covey
story.blurb: Seized in a stable loft before dawn, a young man who has trembled at his tormentor's word for months discovers, mid fight, that he is done trembling.

story.title: Eliza Crosses the Ice
story.blurb: With slave catchers minutes behind her, a mother snatches up her child and runs for the frozen river, where broken ice heaves between her and free ground.
story.spoilerNote: Shows that Eliza's famous escape across the river ice succeeds, defusing the novel's first great chase.

short.title: The Halfpenny Bun
short.blurb: A red haired young man orders his usual halfpenny bun and black coffee, then adds one more item to the order: the shopgirl's hand in marriage.

short.title: The Mouse at Lunchtime
short.blurb: While building a house in the woods, a man is visited each lunchtime by a wild mouse that has never seen a person before.

story.title: A Man Against a Loon
story.blurb: On a calm October pond, a paddler tries to outguess a diving loon whose wild laughter keeps ringing out from wherever he is not looking.

short.title: The Man on the Tower
short.blurb: A young governess on her evening stroll daydreams of meeting a charming stranger on the path, until her imagination suddenly turns real in the wrong place.

story.title: The Man in the Red Sweater
story.blurb: A kidnapped dog, caged and raging for two days, meets a calm man in a red sweater who carries a hatchet and a club.

story.title: The Smiling Blackmailer
story.blurb: A plump, purring gentleman with a frozen smile names his price for a lady's indiscreet letters, and no appeal, threat, or trap can shift him.

story.title: The King of Thieves
story.blurb: A coach tips over a cliff into a flowery hollow so soft it seems providential, and a little priest wonders aloud why they fell just there.
story.spoilerNote: Gives away the courier Ezza's secret identity as the brigand king Montano, a mid story surprise in one of the collection's tales.

story.title: The Walk on the Parapet
story.blurb: A young woman steps onto a tower's narrow parapet to prove she can. The man watching her is not amused, until a slip changes the conversation entirely.
story.spoilerNote: Shows Elfride warming to a second suitor, a courtship the novel develops gradually.

short.title: Laocoön and the Serpents
short.blurb: A priest sacrifices a steer at the shore when two great serpents come gliding over the sea, crests flaming, making straight for him and his young sons.

236.pairNote: Two unrelated tales from the same collection, a mongoose vignette and a wolf-pack council; they coexist fine.

short.title: A Splendid Hunting Ground
short.blurb: A curious young mongoose scouts his splendid new garden, finds a nest of weeping birds, and hears a low cold hiss rise from the thick grass.

story.title: The Council Rock
story.blurb: On a moonlit hilltop, a wolf pack must decide whether a laughing man's cub may run with them, while a tiger roars for his prize in the dark.

story.title: The Word on the Wall
story.blurb: At a murder scene, a proud detective unveils his prize discovery: a word scrawled on the wall in blood. An amateur with a tape measure reads it differently.
story.spoilerNote: Reveals the poison method and the revenge meaning of the bloody word, early deductions though not the killer's identity.

story.title: The Hat Island Crossing
story.blurb: A steamboat races the sunset toward a crossing no pilot dares run in the dark, while every man aboard stands watch in hand, silent.

271.pairNote: Two separate episodes from different points in the horse's life, with no shared text or payoff.

short.title: The First Train
short.blurb: A young horse grazing by the railway meets a rushing, smoking black thing that shrieks and grinds past, and must decide how frightened to stay.

story.title: The Night of the Broken Bridge
story.blurb: Driving home through a wild autumn storm, a horse stops dead at the flooded wooden bridge and will not stir, whatever his master says.

345.pairNote: A castle bedroom and a harbour storm, different narrators and settings with no shared reveal.

short.title: The Shaving Glass
short.blurb: A guest shaving at dawn is startled by his host's greeting; the mirror shows the whole room behind him, and no one else in it.
short.spoilerNote: Tips early that the host is something inhuman, part of the novel's slow-building dread.

story.title: The Derelict in the Storm
story.blurb: A sudden tempest turns a glassy sea into a roaring monster, and watchers on the cliff spot a schooner, all sails set, driving straight for the harbour reef.

short.title: The Man in the Wood
short.blurb: A small boy waiting in a hallway shrieks and collapses in terror. What he points to, once he wakes, has been in the wall all along.
short.spoilerNote: Links the child's terror to an ancient satyr-like presence, pointing toward the novella's central revelation.

story.title: Dinner with an Old Bachelor
story.blurb: Three genteel ladies dine at an old-fashioned farmhouse, where green peas defeat two-pronged forks and their host quotes poetry to the trees.

408.pairNote: Separate autobiographical episodes, one from childhood and one from young manhood, with no overlap.

short.title: A Vast Veil
short.blurb: In a New England schoolhouse, children merrily trade visiting-cards until one glance of refusal shows a boy, all in a day, the world he stands outside.

story.title: The School Behind the Hill
story.blurb: A young teacher tramps the hot Tennessee hills hunting a school of his own, and finds one in a log hut behind a rail fence.
story.brokenNote: The passage cuts off mid-sentence, ending on the dangling words "usually convinced them—for".

421.pairNote: Different scenes on the same journey with no shared text; the short only builds mood the story does not repeat.

short.title: Keep Clear of the Shaws
short.blurb: A lad on the road asks about the great house where he hopes for a place. Every stranger gives him the same wary answer.

story.title: The Unfinished Stair
story.blurb: An old man hands his nephew a rusty key and sends him up an unlit tower stair at night, warning him only to keep to the wall.
story.spoilerNote: Shows early that the uncle means his nephew deadly harm, though the book's larger schemes stay hidden.

story.title: The Visitor at the Seminary
story.blurb: On the day of his triumph in the theology schools, a young man in holy orders receives a caller, the woman who left him two years before.
story.brokenNote: The scene itself is complete, but the final sentence is clipped mid phrase, so the closing declaration ends in the air.

500.pairNote: Back to back episodes with no shared text; the longer one only glances back at the theater scene in passing.

short.title: Take Me Instead
short.blurb: A wooden puppet pleads with the fearsome master of a marionette theater to spare his best friend from the fire.

story.title: The Field of Wonders
story.blurb: A wooden boy with five gold pieces meets a lame Fox and a blind Cat who know of a magic field where money grows overnight.

514.pairNote: Separate scenes, one at a dance and one on the river, with no shared text or shared payoff.

short.title: Behind the Curtain
short.blurb: At a party, a bashful girl slips behind a curtain to hide and finds the boy from next door already there.

story.title: Thin Ice
story.blurb: Refused forgiveness at home, a younger sister chases the skaters down the frozen river, where the ice past the bend has gone soft.

521.pairNote: The wreck and the footprint sit years apart in the tale and share nothing.

short.title: The Footprint in the Sand
short.blurb: Walking to his boat, a castaway long alone finds something pressed into the sand that stops him cold.
short.spoilerNote: Reveals that the island's long solitude is broken, a shock the novel spends years of story building toward.

story.title: Cast Ashore
story.blurb: Eleven men abandon a dying ship in a small boat as mountainous seas drive them toward an unknown shore.

story.title: Her Duty to Go
story.blurb: A daughter dresses for the ball her father has forbidden. Her father is waiting downstairs by the front door.

story.title: The Tread in the Darkness
story.blurb: A stumble in an underground stream leaves an explorer without light in a cave labyrinth. Then he hears footsteps, and they are not human.
story.spoilerNote: Confirms that something real and enormous lives in the cave, a question the full tale keeps in doubt for longer.

551.pairNote: Sequential beats of the same escape; the story assumes the rescue the short depicts but repeats none of it.

short.title: The Face in the Water
short.blurb: Adrift in a lifeboat, a young man leans over the side toward a beautiful face floating on the sea.

story.title: The Tug That Charged
story.blurb: A little tug swings its bow toward a surfaced enemy submarine and rings for full speed. Her crew means to board, with pistols, fists, and one good dog.
story.brokenNote: The battle resolves fully, but the last sentence is clipped mid phrase and visibly trails off.

553.pairNote: Two separate encounters with different creatures; neither steals the other's payoff.

short.title: The Banshee
short.blurb: Five armed men look up from a strange land at something flapping across the sky, and not one of them remembers his rifle.

story.title: Can't Waste Ammunition
story.blurb: When a giant cave bear charges out of a thicket, one man trips in the roots, and the coolest head in the party makes himself the bait.

story.title: The Milkman Trick
story.blurb: With watchers on the street and a body in his rooms, a man stakes his whole escape on the morning milkman.
story.spoilerNote: Reveals the murder of the hero's houseguest, the shock that sets the novel moving, though none of its later secrets.

short.title: The Man Who Wouldn't Fight
short.blurb: A traveler in a grey tweed suit endures a carriage of strangers' contempt for not being at the front, while hiding the reason he cannot answer them.

story.title: Escape by Aeroplane
story.blurb: A fugitive slips into the air in a friend's aeroplane just ahead of the police, tastes the pure joy of flight, then the engine begins to sputter.

story.title: Taken for an Informer
story.blurb: A gentleman who notes down everything takes a cab across London, and his notebook convinces the driver of something sinister enough to start a street brawl.
story.brokenNote: The final sentence is cut off mid-phrase, so the passage ends on an unfinished clause even though the comic arc itself is complete.

short.title: The Lady at the Window
short.blurb: A visitor enters a breakfast room and sees a graceful stranger at the far window; each step she takes toward him revises what he thinks he sees.

story.title: A Touch at Midnight
story.blurb: On a lonely road at one in the morning, a hand falls on a walker's shoulder, and a woman dressed all in white asks the way to London.

story.title: The Duel in Hunter's Bog
story.blurb: A leering stranger picks a quarrel, blow answers insult, and a young man who has never learned to fence must walk to a duel he expects to lose.

story.title: The Bowl of Rack Punch
story.blurb: At a pleasure garden, one bowl of punch proves too tempting for a vain gourmand, and an evening that should have settled a marriage goes gloriously sideways.

short.title: Treated Like a Fly
short.blurb: A man sunk in depression walks into a tavern half hoping to be thrown out of a window, and receives an insult far harder to forgive.

story.title: Look at the Sheets
story.blurb: A whispered warning from the woodman's wife sends a traveler to check his bed, and what he finds keeps him listening in the dark at the window.

short.title: Asking for More
short.blurb: In a workhouse where boys starve on thin gruel, lots are cast, and one small desperate child must walk up to the master and ask for more.

story.title: A Word Against His Mother
story.blurb: A charity-boy bully needles a quiet orphan at dinner, prodding and jeering until he finds the one subject that turns the mild child to fire.

story.title: His Formidable Aunt
story.blurb: A boy who has walked for days, robbed and sleeping in fields, gathers his last courage to introduce himself to an aunt famous for chasing boys away.
story.spoilerNote: It reveals that the narrator's mother has died, a loss the full book only reaches after several chapters.

short.title: Let Me In
short.blurb: Kept awake by a branch tapping the glass, a sleeper breaks the pane to silence it, and his fingers close on something that grips back.

story.title: The Lighted Window
story.blurb: Two wild children run barefoot through the dark to spy on a rich family's bright window, laughing at what they see, until the bulldog is let loose.

short.title: Six Inches High
short.blurb: A man wakes flat on his back, unable to stir, every limb tied down. Then something alive, six inches tall, comes marching up his chest.

short.title: Cigars in the Coal Scuttle
short.blurb: A doctor shares rooms with a brilliant friend who keeps cigars in the coal scuttle, tobacco in a slipper, and does pistol practice indoors. A fond, exasperated portrait.

844.pairNote: Two separate tea-time scenes with the same cast; the sandwich vignette and the interview stand apart without repeating or resolving each other.

short.title: Not Even for Ready Money
short.blurb: An aunt arrives for tea expecting the cucumber sandwiches she was promised. There are none, not even for ready money, and the excuses are exquisite.

story.title: The Handbag Interview
story.blurb: A formidable mother interviews a hopeful suitor: income, politics, parents. His answers go beautifully until she asks who his people are, and he must mention a handbag.

story.title: The Tenth of February
story.blurb: At sunrise, gunfire wakes a frontier town. From inside a burning house, a mother watches neighbors fall and must walk out through the smoke with her children.

story.title: Behind the Locked Door
story.blurb: In the small hours a household wakes to alarming sounds behind a locked bedroom door. The doors will not give, and the lady inside is very ill.

910.pairNote: The longer piece openly explains the riddle the short one turns on: a seventh animal that comes in at feeding time is the wolf pack's decoy.

short.title: One Fish Short
short.blurb: Two men and six sled dogs camp in the frozen dark. At feeding time Bill counts the animals that came for fish, and the number is wrong.

story.title: Wolves at the Firelight
story.blurb: Wolves shadow two men across the frozen dark, and each night the circle draws in. A doglike shape slides into the firelight, watching the dogs, not the men.

story.title: The Marksman in the Oak
story.blurb: A rifle shot comes from an impossible direction. High in a ragged oak across the river, a marksman is hidden, and the men below must bring him down.

967.pairNote: One is a coach-stop vignette, the other the schoolroom revolt weeks later; neither repeats or spoils the other's turn.

short.title: Nothing, Please Sir
short.blurb: A small boy perched on a trunk commits the crime of sneezing. His schoolmaster's response, in a public coffee room, says everything about the school ahead.

story.title: The Schoolmaster Meets His Match
story.blurb: A runaway boy is dragged back to be flogged before the whole school. The new young assistant sits at his desk, and something in his face is different.

story.title: Called to Account
story.blurb: A stout, sleepy secret agent is summoned to the Embassy and dressed down by a new master who wants activity. The agent has one talent left to show.

1001.pairNote: Two different stops on the same descent; the gateway and the lovers share nothing but the traveler.

short.title: Abandon All Hope
short.blurb: A traveler reads the dreadful inscription over a dark gateway, then passes through into starless air full of sighs, led by a guide who knows the way.

story.title: Paolo and Francesca
story.blurb: In a black wind that never rests, whirled spirits cry out. Two of them drift close, still together, and one tells how a shared book undid them.

short.title: Stuck in the Railings
short.blurb: A visitor arrives at a chaotic household to find a small boy wedged by the neck between iron railings, and everyone's rescue plan makes it worse.

1063.pairNote: The short is the carnival lure and the story is the descent that follows; contiguous scenes but no shared text and no shared payoff.

short.title: Luckily Met at Carnival
short.blurb: At the height of carnival, a man in motley is flattered into abandoning the festivities to prove his palate against a rival's, whatever the cold vaults hold.

story.title: Down Among the Bones
story.blurb: Two friends descend by torchlight through bone-lined vaults in search of a rare wine, one coughing in the damp, the other oddly solicitous about turning back.
story.spoilerNote: The trowel moment strongly telegraphs what the narrator plans for his companion in the vaults.

short.title: The Corporal Drops His Hat
short.blurb: News of a death reaches the kitchen, and a corporal's single gesture with his hat says more about mortality than any sermon.

short.title: The Headless Ones
short.blurb: From a hidden vantage, a traveler watches headless human bodies crawl and feed inside a walled enclosure, and slowly realizes this is their normal condition.
short.spoilerNote: Reveals the headless creatures the heroine discovers early in the book, though not what they truly are.

story.title: Two Simple Words
story.blurb: A broke young woman interviews for a suspiciously generous job in Paris, and a name plucked from memory turns her genial employer purple with rage.

short.title: In the Name of the Law
short.blurb: Three blows at the door interrupt a gathering, and a magistrate with soldiers asks which of the company answers to a certain name.

short.title: A Most Violent Knocking
short.blurb: A family round their fireside hears a thunderous knocking and must debate, at length and with great philosophy, whether anyone is actually at the door.

short.title: The Mantle of Kings' Beards
short.blurb: A messenger brings an outrageous demand: a rival king trims his mantle with the beards of conquered kings, and one place remains.

story.title: The Kitchen Knight
story.blurb: A damosel begs the court for a champion and storms off when the quest goes to a kitchen page. Then he starts unhorsing famous knights.

short.title: The Siege of the Cellar
short.blurb: A barricaded friend finally opens the cellar door, upright but swaying, having spent his siege drinking the innkeeper's stock down to the last cask.

story.title: Four Against Five
story.blurb: A young hothead must choose a side in seconds when three outnumbered swordsmen face the cardinal's guards, and the choice will cost blood.

story.title: One of the Forty Ways
story.blurb: A captive duke entertains his jailer by describing, step by step, exactly how a prisoner might escape, while a pie sits waiting on the table.
story.spoilerNote: Shows that the duke's long-planned escape from the fortress succeeds.

short.title: How Dare I
short.blurb: Trembling but unstoppable, a small girl finally tells the woman who raised her exactly what her coldness and cruelty have cost, and what she will tell the world.

short.title: Thirty Miles to Land
short.blurb: A storm-driven balloon sinks toward furious waves with land in sight; its passengers cling to the net and count the miles as the gas runs out.

story.title: Mr. Collins's Proposal
story.blurb: A pompous clergyman proposes marriage with his reasons numbered and his patroness quoted; the lady refuses plainly, but refusal is not an answer he recognizes.
story.brokenNote: The text cuts off mid-sentence on a dangling comma in Mr. Collins's final reply.

story.title: England Can Afford It
story.blurb: A catastrophe has left thirteen soldiers on a shrunken island where days last six hours; the two officers in charge calmly finish their chess move and settle the men's pay.
story.spoilerNote: It sketches the strange physical changes to the world whose cause the full book stages as a slow-dawning mystery.

short.title: A Glance Between Strangers
short.blurb: Stepping aside at a carriage door, an officer glances at a lady and must look again; something in her face keeps escaping her control.

story.title: The Steeplechase
story.blurb: Before the Tsar and all the crowd, an officer and his beloved mare fly the barriers together, a rival's hoofbeats never fading behind them.

story.title: Twenty Minutes to Nine
story.blurb: A boy is sent to play in a candlelit house where daylight never enters, before a lady in a yellowed bridal dress whose clocks stopped long ago.

short.title: Taken with a Maid
short.blurb: Arrested for being caught with a girl, a country clown disputes every word of the royal proclamation, from wench to damsel to maid.

story.title: Four Woodcocks in a Dish
story.blurb: A lord who swore an oath against love hides to watch his king and two friends, one by one, read aloud the sonnets they should never have written.

1513.pairNote: Consecutive beats of one courtship, but the ball's banter and the balcony's vows each land on their own.

short.title: Two Blushing Pilgrims
short.blurb: At a masked feast, a stranger takes a girl's hand and turns one touch into a playful theology of saints and pilgrims; then he learns whose daughter she is.

story.title: The Balcony Scene
story.blurb: From a dark orchard, a young man overhears the girl he loves asking the night why a name should stand between them, and steps out to answer.

story.title: The Sharp Athenian Law
story.blurb: A father hauls his daughter before the duke, demanding an old law: wed the suitor he chose or die. Left alone, the lovers make another plan.
story.brokenNote: Cuts off mid-sentence in Hermia's closing vow ('Tomorrow truly will'), leaving the ending hanging in the air.

short.title: Hercules Be Thy Speed
short.blurb: An unknown young man insists on wrestling the duke's fearsome champion while two ladies cheer him on; his father's name matters more than anyone expects.

story.title: A Cure for Love
story.blurb: Deep in the forest, a quick-tongued youth corners the poet who hangs love rhymes on trees and prescribes a strange cure: woo me as your Rosalind.

1564.pairNote: Two separate anecdotes from the same friendship, years apart; neither repeats or flattens the other.

short.title: I Do Indeed Come from Scotland
short.blurb: A nervous young Scot finally meets the literary giant he reveres, and his very first sentence hands the famous wit a perfect opening.

story.title: The Dinner with Jack Wilkes
story.blurb: A determined young matchmaker of enemies tricks a great moralist into dining with the scandalous politician he loathes, then watches nervously from across the table.

story.title: The Swineherd
story.blurb: A scorned prince disguises himself as a palace pigkeeper and sets an unusual price on his ingenious toys: kisses from the princess who rejected him.

story.title: Devotion
story.blurb: At a late supper party, a young man follows a beautiful, ailing courtesan from the table and offers her the one thing she refuses to believe in.

story.title: Down Upper Swandam Lane
story.blurb: Sent to fetch a friend home from a riverside opium den at midnight, a doctor feels a pluck at his sleeve and a whisper: walk past, then look back.

1685.pairNote: An arrival scene and a midnight stakeout from different points in the investigation; no shared text or shared payoff.

short.title: The Ungloved Hand
short.blurb: A young reporter arrives at a chateau, stares at his host's gloved hands, and refuses to shake until he sees what the gloves conceal.

story.title: The Man at the Desk
story.blurb: Midnight at a guarded chateau: a young reporter climbs a ladder to a lit window and finds an intruder calmly writing at the victim's desk.
story.spoilerNote: It hints that the attacked woman knows her assailant and is shielding him, a question the full book unwinds slowly.

short.title: The Turning Key
short.blurb: Two watchers keep a silent vigil over a sleeping general when a key turns softly in the lock and an arm reaches through the dark.

1695.pairNote: Back-to-back scenes from the same night; the story picks up soon after the short's ominous closing line, but neither repeats the other's punch.

short.title: The Lamp and the Tree
short.blurb: A poet waits rigid as a statue beneath a street lamp at night, determined to end an argument about order and anarchy once and for all.

story.title: The Lobster and the Bombs
story.blurb: In a greasy beershop, a poet orders champagne and lobster for his guest, then politely warns him not to be alarmed if the table begins to turn.

story.title: The Harp in the Danish Camp
story.blurb: A defeated king lays down his sword, takes up an old harp, and walks unarmed into the firelit camp of the invaders to sing for them.

story.title: Noman and the Cyclops
story.blurb: Trapped in a man-eating giant's cave, a cunning captain sharpens a beam of olive wood, pours strong wine, and gives a very careful answer about his name.

1747.pairNote: A courtroom scene and a later break-in scuffle; separate incidents with separate shocks.

short.title: A Hand in the Dark
short.blurb: Letting himself into a friend's dark apartment at night, a man reaches for the light switch and closes his fingers over warm flesh.

story.title: Morning in the Police Court
story.blurb: A ragged burglar caught hiding in a coat closet stands before the judge, while the volunteer lawyer defending him grows strangely uneasy.

1837.pairNote: One stages the clothes swap, the other plays out a comic consequence at court; they complement without repeating.

short.title: No Hereditary Scratcher
short.blurb: A boy dining before a solemn court is seized by an itch, and nothing in English history offers guidance on what to do next.

story.title: Rags and Splendours
story.blurb: A little prince and a beggar boy trade stories of their worlds, then trade clothes for a lark, and a mirror shows them something strange.

short.title: Go Back to Lenox
short.blurb: An old man arrives at a hotel trailing his vanished wife and finds a letter already waiting, four words scrawled in a peculiar shade of yellow pencil.

story.title: Dear Madman
story.blurb: A gentleman of independent means picks his professions, and his railway stops, purely on whim. His latest stop lands him at a friend's door at exactly the wrong moment.

story.title: Six Red Flags
story.blurb: The hillside slides down onto the railway line, and three children with seven minutes and nothing red must find a way to warn the 11.29.
story.brokenNote: The final sentence is cut off in the middle of its phrase, ending on 'the sticks of the little red', a visible truncation right at the emotional climax.

1931.pairNote: The hat found in one is the hat lost in the other; the link enriches both rather than repeating a payoff.

short.title: The Trophy Hat
short.blurb: A freckled schoolgirl bursts in waving a gentleman's hat found where the enemy airship passed over, and she is not about to surrender it to anyone.

story.title: A Letter of Introduction
story.blurb: A muddy stranger climbs through a lady's library window, apologizes beautifully, blocks her way to the bell, and seems to know exactly who everyone is.

short.title: A Yellow Smell
short.blurb: In a damp week the smell arrives, creeping through every room of the house, hanging over her bed at night. She cannot name it, but she keeps trying.
short.spoilerNote: The rubbed streak round the room quietly foreshadows the tale's closing revelation without explaining it.

story.title: The Woman Behind the Pattern
story.blurb: By moonlight the wallpaper pattern shakes. She begs her doctor husband to take her away; he knows better, of course. So she keeps watching.
story.spoilerNote: Reveals the woman behind the pattern, a development the full tale builds to gradually, though the ending stays hidden.

short.title: A Voice in the Dark
short.blurb: An officers' mess drowses through a hot evening of engagement talk until a tired voice lifts out of the darkness, asking for her husband.

short.title: The Immortal Druggist
short.blurb: On a wet London Sunday a man steps into a chemist's shop and comes to believe the dull fellow behind the counter is no mortal at all.

story.title: The Pensive Citadel
story.blurb: At half past three on a July morning a schoolboy rises to run away, pausing to kiss a picture goodbye and smuggle a mighty trunk past his headmaster's door.

short.title: The Trick With the Old Hat
short.blurb: A schoolboy learns from an older boy that a certain old hat, moved just so, buys cakes for free in any shop in town.

story.title: The Brother's Watch
story.blurb: To puncture his friend's dogmatic streak, a doctor hands over a newly cleaned pocket watch and asks what can possibly be read from it.

story.title: The Chain of Thought
story.blurb: On a night walk through Paris, a man answers his companion's silent thoughts aloud, then retraces every link of the invisible chain that led him there.

short.title: The Sealed Abbey
short.blurb: A plague empties the countryside, its whole course half an hour. A prince gathers a thousand friends behind welded iron gates and provides every pleasure.

story.title: The Cask of Amontillado
story.blurb: During carnival's madness, a man nursing a secret grudge dangles a rare wine before a connoisseur in motley and leads him down into the family catacombs.

short.title: Hector and Andromache
short.blurb: A warrior in full armour reaches for his baby son, who shrieks at the nodding plume of his helmet. Laughter, a prayer, and a farewell follow.

short.title: But Why Turkish?
short.blurb: A detective glances at his friend's boots and asks an impossible question. Pressed to explain his method, he starts instead with mud splashes on a coat sleeve.

short.title: The Clock and the Cap
short.blurb: A boy working at a furnace nudges the clock hands forward each morning to make it to school, then faces a second problem: every other child wears a hat.

story.title: Fifty Cents and a Broom
story.blurb: Penniless in a strange city, a young traveler sleeps under a board sidewalk and unloads pig iron, still set on reaching the school of his dreams.

short.title: Who Put Salt in the Water?
short.blurb: A child springs into the surf without fear until a wave pulls the ground away. Rescued and furious, she has one burning question about the sea.

story.title: Everything Has a Name
story.blurb: A wordless child meets the stranger who spells letters into her hand. The finger game means nothing to her until one morning beside the water spout.

story.title: Letting Her Go
story.blurb: A corporal marches a beautiful prisoner to jail through winding streets. She drops her mantilla, guesses his home country, and begins to speak his language.

short.title: A Bedfellow with a Tomahawk
short.blurb: In a dark inn room, a traveler's unknown bedfellow climbs in with a tomahawk pipe between his teeth. Neither man can make himself understood.

story.title: The Waltz and the Storm
story.blurb: A young man waltzes at a country ball with a girl who dances with her whole heart, until a smiling stranger wags a finger and repeats one name.

2542.pairNote: Two separate confrontations from different acts with no shared text or shared payoff.

short.title: Silk Stockings
short.blurb: A wife shows a family friend the silk stockings she will wear tomorrow. His answers keep drifting toward a farewell she refuses to hear.
short.spoilerNote: Hints that Doctor Rank is near death, a thread the play unfolds gradually.

story.title: A Discrepancy in the Date
story.blurb: A man about to lose his post at the bank calls on the wife of the man dismissing him. He has a paper, and questions about a date.
story.spoilerNote: Reveals Nora's secret loan and forged signature, the discovery that drives the entire play.

story.title: A Drop of Water
story.blurb: Chained to the pillory, a deaf man endures the crowd's stones and jeers. He begs for a drink, and the last person he expects climbs the ladder.

short.title: The Last Five Minutes
short.blurb: A condemned man, given five minutes before execution, divides them carefully: farewells, reflection, one last look. A sunlit church spire holds his gaze until the end.

story.title: Something Tremendous Has Happened
story.blurb: At dusk in an Italian square, a young woman sees a stabbing and faints into the arms of a man she hardly knows. The walk home changes something.
story.spoilerNote: Signals the bond forming between the two leads, a connection the novel keeps in suspense.

short.title: Gold for the White Whale
short.blurb: A captain holds a Spanish gold coin up to the sun and nails it to the mast, promising it to whoever first sights a certain white whale.

story.title: Kings of Kafiristan
story.blurb: Two sunburnt loafers walk into a newspaper office at four in the morning with maps to borrow and a plan: march into a wild mountain country and crown themselves kings.

short.title: Something in the Cream Puff
short.blurb: In a grand hotel dining room, a watchful young woman sees an elegant Baroness quietly take something out of her dessert that should not be there.
short.spoilerNote: Shows the Baroness slipping in her fake accent, flagging early the disguise the novel later unmasks.

2825.pairNote: Separate scenes with no shared text; the short's soul confession is not the flood story's payoff.

short.title: The Girl Without a Soul
short.blurb: On her wedding evening, a laughing girl tells the priest she has no soul, then asks through tears whether such a gift is lovely or terrible.
short.spoilerNote: States outright that she has no soul, the secret of her nature that the book reveals just after the wedding.

story.title: The Island in the Flood
story.blurb: A storm has cut the peninsula off from the world, and a knight wades into the midnight flood, warned off by a voice in the water, to find a girl lost in it.

story.title: The Splendid Security
story.blurb: An English lord lays his heart, his lands, and the whole world's climates at a young American woman's feet. She likes him immensely. And yet.
story.spoilerNote: Implies she will refuse this eligible suitor, settling early one of the novel's open questions.

story.title: David and Goliath
story.blurb: A giant in brass armor taunts an army for forty days, until a shepherd boy carrying provisions to his brothers decides someone should answer him.

story.title: A Hound of Hell
story.blurb: A wild and godless squire carries off a yeoman's daughter. When she escapes across the moonlit moor, he swears his soul to the Powers of Evil and rides.

story.title: The Crate Came Alone
story.blurb: A precious mummy case arrives without the assistant who guarded it across the sea. As an impatient professor pries off the lid, an old woman asks where her boy is.
story.spoilerNote: Reveals the murder discovery that launches the novel's mystery, though nothing of who did it or why.

short.title: The Stag at Eve
short.blurb: A stag wakes at dawn to hounds and horns on the mountain. The whole glen erupts as the chase sweeps past, then fades into silence.

short.title: Fire in the Thatch
short.blurb: Thatch blazes faster than water can touch it, and one man vanishes into the burning inn. Neighbors force the door against the flames to bring him out.
short.spoilerNote: Reveals that the inn burns down, an event the novel stages as a dramatic turn in its central mystery.

3070.pairNote: One is the ancient family legend and the other the modern death it haunts; they share no text and neither gives away the other's payoff.

short.title: The Marks Beside the Body
short.blurb: A country doctor recounts the night he examined a dead man whose face was convulsed with fear, then lowers his voice to name what he found nearby.

story.title: The Curse of the Baskervilles
story.blurb: An old manuscript tells how a wicked squire carried off a farmer's daughter, and what came running over the moonlit moor on the night she fled.

3146.pairNote: A starlit conversation and a secret wedding from different stretches of the book; nothing shared, nothing deflated.

short.title: The Terrible Science
short.blurb: Under the open night sky, a young astronomer argues that the stars offer not wonder but horror: sizes beyond awe, and lights already dying.

story.title: Five Minutes to Eleven
story.blurb: Two lovers slip into a near-empty church to be married in secret, fearing every passing glance. The parson is late, and she begins to read omens.
story.spoilerNote: Shows that the astronomer and the lady marry in secret, a development the novel spends chapters building toward.

story.title: The Genuine Mexican Plug
story.blurb: A newcomer to a frontier town, dazzled by the local horsemanship, bids on an auction horse with one remarkable talent. A stranger's whisper closes the sale.

story.title: The Bodymaster's Welcome
story.blurb: A cocky newcomer elbows through a crowded saloon to introduce himself to its dangerous owner, and the interview swings from banter to a drawn revolver.

story.title: First Night Out
story.blurb: Fresh from prison, a quick-tongued schemer settles an old score on a dark pier, then climbs the stairs to dinner and finds a girl all grown up.

story.title: Through the Zone of Fire
story.blurb: Becalmed over dark villages as a tropical tempest gathers, three balloonists must choose: drop toward the trees or climb straight through the lightning.

short.title: Voices in the Granite
short.blurb: Lost in absolute darkness deep underground, a weakened wanderer presses his ear to the rock and catches what cannot possibly be there: words.

story.title: Sigurd's Cavern
story.blurb: Deep in a torchlit cavern, an English traveler meets its keeper, a misshapen dwarf with wild blue eyes who says the dead have summoned him across the sea.
story.spoilerNote: Sigurd's prophecy hints early at the book's central romance and foreshadows how his own devotion to Thelma will end.

short.title: The Worst Dancer at Court
short.blurb: Asked if he dances well, a young courtier answers with confidence. At the royal ball, before the King himself, he gets his chance to prove it.

story.title: The King's Farewell
story.blurb: An old king, dying in state, calls his court to his bedside: cardinals, princes, weeping duchesses, and at last a small child who will inherit everything.

story.title: The Affair of the Necklace
story.blurb: A jeweller arrives at a lady's country house demanding payment for a fabulous necklace the Queen insists she never bought. Someone is lying, and the sums are ruinous.

story.title: The Concert of Monsieur Vaussore
story.blurb: A penniless young wanderer reinvents himself as a Parisian music master, though he cannot read a note. Then a professor asks him to compose a piece for his concert.

story.title: The Examination at Surgeons' Hall
story.blurb: A trembling young Scot faces a dozen grim examiners for his surgeon's licence, fielding trick questions until his judges start quarrelling among themselves.

story.title: The Great Fire
story.blurb: Woken at three in the morning by a maid's report of a fire, a London official goes back to sleep. By daylight, the whole riverfront is burning.

story.title: Waiting for the Overt Act
story.blurb: February 1917: a cabinet secretary writes a friend in confidence, recording what the President says behind closed doors as German submarines push a neutral nation toward war.

4300.pairNote: Adjacent slices of the same Dublin morning, but they share no text and each has its own payoff.

short.title: Milk for the Pussens
short.blurb: A gentle man moves softly about his kitchen at breakfast time, sizing up his black cat as she sizes up him.

story.title: Tea and Metempsychosis
story.blurb: He carries the breakfast tray up to his wife, answers her question about a strange word, and tries not to think about the letter under her pillow.

short.title: The Price of the Colt
short.blurb: A boy of eight wants a neighbour's colt so badly that his father finally lets him ride over and bargain for it himself.

story.title: First Day Under Fire
story.blurb: A young lieutenant advances through tall prairie grass into his first battle, watching cannon balls ricochet slowly enough to dodge, and learning what war actually does.

short.title: A Distant View of Wilsonople
short.blurb: A complacent General opens a letter from Italy and finds it composed of ink sketches of a city called Wilsonople. Page by page, they grow alarmingly personal.

story.title: The Earl and the Bull
story.blurb: A timid young clerk hears shouting from a pasture: an elderly earl is holding off a charging bull with nothing but a garden spud.

story.title: The Man Who Called Himself Farr
story.blurb: A sunburnt stranger in vagrant's clothes strolls a June road, baffling a constable, rescuing a stalled motorcar, and trading looks with a girl who remembers to say please.

story.title: The Dandelion Clock
story.blurb: Alone by the bridge, a girl blows dandelion seeds to divine a stranger's age. On the very last puff, a shadow falls across the grass.

short.title: The Eve of Waterloo
short.blurb: Brussels dances by lamplight, a thousand hearts beating happily, when a deep sound rolls in from the distance. Some say it is only the wind.

story.title: The Sacred Goose
story.blurb: Three sacred geese ambush a temple guest, and he fights back with a table leg. The priestess returns to find her darling dead and her house polluted.

story.title: The Widow of Ephesus
story.blurb: A widow famed for devotion vows to starve in her husband's tomb. Nearby, a soldier guarding crucified thieves notices a light among the graves.

short.title: Da Capo!
short.blurb: After a rehearsal so wretched he nearly stays home, a young composer goes to his symphony's premiere, resolved to seize the first violin himself if things go wrong.

story.title: Shelter from the Storm
story.blurb: A sudden storm drives three drenched walkers to a bachelor's gate. He lights the kitchen fire, pours brandy, and hands round tea while the thunder does its work.

story.title: A Wedding in the Dark
story.blurb: On a quiet Sunday evening a young governess learns her wedding is to happen at once, in a darkened room, to a bridegroom who cannot bear the light.
story.spoilerNote: Reveals that the heroine's secret marriage to the unseen recluse takes place, a mid-book development, though the deeper mystery of the bridegroom stays intact.

story.title: The Undoer of Wrongs
story.blurb: A knight-errant follows cries into a thicket, where a farmer flogs a shepherd boy. Justice is pronounced, sworn to, and left to keep itself.

story.title: Hector and Andromache
story.blurb: A warrior slips home from the battle to find his wife and infant son at the city gate. She begs him to stay; he answers with what honor demands.
story.spoilerNote: Hector's forebodings of his own death and Troy's fall point toward the epic's ending, though the poem itself announces both throughout.

short.title: A Letter From Prison
short.blurb: A country baron signs for a registered letter and reads, in flawless courtesy, a list of his own treasures and an eight-day deadline.

story.title: The Passenger List
story.blurb: Word spreads that a famous burglar is aboard a transatlantic steamer, traveling under a name beginning with R. The passengers turn detective, and the jewels start disappearing.

story.title: The Night Climb
story.blurb: The tide is out and the moon is up as a sailor sets his fingers to a cliff no one has climbed, with a girl's voice calling from below.

short.title: The Churchyard Battle
short.blurb: A village mob turns on one young woman in a churchyard, and she answers with a skull and a thigh-bone, in the grandest epic style.

short.title: Race to the Crossing
short.blurb: Two riders tear toward the city at a mad gallop until a train whistle and a falling crossing gate stop everything at once.

story.title: Eleven Nickels
story.blurb: A ragged small boy with a crowbar breaks into a saloon after dark, bent on settling accounts with the machine that swallowed his nickels.

6768.pairNote: Two separate stories from the same collection; neither touches the other.

short.title: Falling for a Swimmer
short.blurb: A well-brought-up young man knows staring is rude, but the girl swimming past the pier is a special case, and the railing is only so high.

story.title: The Knocking From Above
story.blurb: A composer at her piano keeps hearing a boot-heel banging on the ceiling. She marches upstairs to crush the brute responsible.

story.title: The Pike and the Lady
story.blurb: A young fisherman hooks the pike of a lifetime just as a beautiful stranger kneels on the bank to help, with dragoons on the road behind her.

story.title: Flight Toward the Himalayas
story.blurb: Three schoolboys in new English clothes slip away by train toward the mountains, hoping for masters and cosmic consciousness, with a clever older brother on their trail.

story.title: The Highwayman's Prescription
story.blurb: Three highwaymen stop a nobleman's carriage on a frosty road. What follows is less a robbery than a duel of perfect manners.

short.title: The Prince of the Air
short.blurb: In an old count's papers, a traveling scholar finds a recipe for long life that begins with a pilgrimage to Chorazin. He finds himself lingering by the mausoleum.
short.spoilerNote: It reveals the count's secret occult pilgrimage, which the full tale uncovers gradually, though the story's ending stays untouched.

short.title: The Marble Lily
short.blurb: A friend drops an Easter lily into a basin of strange liquid. What he lifts out is flawless marble, veined faintly blue, with a flush deep in its heart.

8800.pairNote: Two separate visions from different circles of the same journey; neither contains the other's payoff.

short.title: Abandon All Hope
short.blurb: Two travelers pass beneath a portal carved with terrible words, into starless air loud with sighs, and one asks his guide who these wailing souls are.

story.title: Paolo and Francesca
story.blurb: A ceaseless black wind whirls spirits like flocks of starlings. Two who fly together, light upon the storm, descend to tell how love brought them here.

short.title: The Secret Drawer
short.blurb: Left alone with their mistress's jewels, a maid and her sweetheart press a hidden knob, and what springs out is worth more to her than any diamond.
short.spoilerNote: Shows that the lady of the house secretly keeps a baby's shoe and lock of hair, an early planted clue to her hidden past.

short.title: Danusia's Knight
short.blurb: When a bench tips and a little singer totters, a young squire springs like a wildcat to catch her, and a laughing princess names him her knight.

9911.pairNote: The toast is the insult that provokes the duel, but each scene keeps its own payoff.

short.title: The Officer's Toast
short.blurb: A drunken officer rises, glass in hand, to toast the prettiest girl in the room and take the rose beside her plate. Her look alone answers him.

story.title: The Duel in the Clearing
story.blurb: In a flowered clearing outside town, two young men face each other with pistols, while a terrified old second hides behind a bush to shout the count.

10002.pairNote: Both feature the same swine creatures, a first sighting and a later attack, but each scene has its own payoff.

short.title: The Face at the Window
short.blurb: Reading after dinner, a man glances up to see eyes and ears above the window ledge. He takes it for a pig. It is no pig.

story.title: The Creatures from the Pit
story.blurb: A crash from the Pit sends dust boiling into the evening sky. A man takes his gun to the edge and looks down at what is climbing out.

story.title: The Stranger on the Bridge
story.blurb: Two proud men meet midway on a log bridge over a pebbly stream, and neither will give way. Staves are cut, and the question must be settled.

10441.pairNote: Separate comic episodes with different characters and different payoffs.

short.title: The Impossible Mice
short.blurb: She has heard squeals in the walls and means to write to the landlord. Then, out of the wainscoting, comes a single file of mice in colors mice never wear.

story.title: The Runaway Elevator
story.blurb: A maid mistakes a young man's camera case for a doctor's bag and runs him home to her mistress. The ornate house elevator has plans of its own.

short.title: New Year on the Auction Block
short.blurb: While others keep holiday, a mother sits on a cold cabin floor, watching children who may be taken from her by morning. A witness sets down what she saw.

story.title: A Letter from New York
story.blurb: From a cramped hiding place, a runaway writes a letter for a trusted sailor to post far away, then waits, silent behind a door, to hear her hunter read it.

11339.pairNote: Different fables entirely, with no shared text.

short.title: The Buffoon and the Countryman
short.blurb: A clown brings the theatre down with his imitation of a pig's squeal. A countryman swears he can do better, and hides something under his smock.
short.brokenNote: The text ends mid-sentence on a comma, cutting off the countryman's closing retort that is the fable's point.

story.title: A Handful of Fables
story.blurb: A flattered crow, a wolf hunting for an excuse, a blind woman with a clever defense, and a god testing an honest woodman. Small tales with sharp points.

11982.pairNote: Two separate childhood episodes from the same memoir; no shared text or payoff.

short.title: The Swapped Composition
short.blurb: A schoolgirl trades her clever composition for a friend's dull one, then watches the exchange unravel in front of the whole school.

story.title: A Girl as Good as a Boy
story.blurb: After her brother's death, an eleven-year-old girl vows to be everything a son could be: Greek before breakfast, fences on horseback, all to earn one sentence from her father.

story.title: I'll Try This Case Myself
story.blurb: A mild-seeming judge starts asking questions nobody expects, and two shyster lawyers and a crooked policeman feel the courtroom floor tilt under them.
story.spoilerNote: Shows the courtroom collapse of the frame-up against Tony, which is the payoff of one story in the collection.

story.title: The Sugar Corner
story.blurb: Three hundred picked men wait for the gong on the Exchange floor. The calmest face in the middle of the mob is about to set the market on fire.

12758.pairNote: Two unrelated tales from the anthology; nothing shared.

short.title: The Drum of the Sands
short.blurb: Crossing a sea of burning sand, a caravan halts: somewhere among the dunes an invisible drum begins to roll, and the guides whisper of death.

story.title: An Uncomfortable Bed
story.blurb: A guest at a chateau full of practical jokers lies awake certain a prank is coming, and takes elaborate precautions against every trick he can imagine.

story.title: The Hair of Gold
story.blurb: A knight lands disguised in a hostile country, fights a fire-breathing dragon alone, and wakes to find his life in the hands of the woman he came to win.
story.spoilerNote: Reveals the hero's hidden identity as the Morholt's slayer and how he wins the princess from the false seneschal, an early staged discovery of the legend.

14471.pairNote: Drawn from two different ghost stories in the collection; nothing shared.

short.title: Footsteps on the Stair
short.blurb: Alone at night by his open door, a student hears boots climbing the spiral staircase toward him, loud and close, long before anyone comes into view.

story.title: The Search at Midnight
story.blurb: A man and his elderly aunt search an empty house at midnight, room by room and floor by floor, and the house begins to answer back.

story.title: The Knock in the Blizzard
story.blurb: Midnight, a howling blizzard, and a pounding at the front door. A small-town couple in their nightclothes argue over who has to answer it.

story.title: Errour's Den
story.blurb: Warned by his lady and begged by his dwarf to fly, a young knight walks into a monster's den anyway, his glimmering armor the only light.

short.title: Hooked
short.blurb: An angler swerves politely around a rival's cast at dusk and takes the fly in his ear. The stranger holding the rod is not what he expected.

story.title: Put Off in the Rain
story.blurb: A conductor demands a fare she has already paid. The girl refuses, the rain roars down, and a stranger's gloved hand starts gathering her scattered note-books.

short.title: First Snow
short.blurb: A boy of twelve, newly arrived in England, finds the ship's deck white overnight and runs to tell the mate that someone has thrown salt everywhere.

story.title: Struck Upon the Rocks
story.blurb: A sailor dreams of shipwreck three nights running, then spots the rock himself. When the sloop strikes, the captain gives an order that could doom everyone below deck.

16389.pairNote: Consecutive scenes in the book, the night walk then the next morning, but each carries its own payoff.

short.title: Opening the Shutters
short.blurb: A woman wakes in a castle bedroom in Italy, throws open the shutters, and finds more beauty waiting than she knows how to hold.

story.title: Arrival by Lantern Light
story.blurb: Two Englishwomen, stranded at night in Italy with no Italian, must follow a stranger with a lantern down steps and along a dark quay toward a castle they cannot see.

short.title: His Grandfather's Bed
short.blurb: A small, immaculate man travels far to sleep in his grandfather's bed, and sits down to supper among four giant sons who dwarf everyone but his talk.

story.title: Bound by Tiny Hands
story.blurb: A traveller wakes flat on his back, arms, legs, and hair pinned to the ground, as something alive and six inches tall marches up his chest.

short.title: The Snow Child
short.blurb: A merchant comes home after ten years abroad to find a young son, and his wife has a perfectly calm explanation involving a leaf of sorrel and snow.

story.title: Dead Drunk
story.blurb: A drunk Dutchman corners a priest, demands confession at knifepoint, receives absolution, and then decides the sensible next step is to die at once and go straight to heaven.

short.title: The Sea Below the World
short.blurb: Deep underground, a traveller opens his dazzled eyes on something impossible: a limitless sea breaking on golden sand beneath a roof of rock.
short.spoilerNote: Reveals the discovery of the vast underground sea, one of the book's central wonders.
short.brokenNote: The last sentence breaks off unfinished ('the mighty rocks faded away like'), so the ending is visibly truncated.

story.title: A Battle of Monsters
story.blurb: On a raft far from any shore, three travellers are jolted awake as two enormous creatures from a vanished age circle their vessel and then turn on each other.
story.spoilerNote: Gives away the famous prehistoric sea monster battle and which creature wins.

story.title: The Man Under the Straw
story.blurb: Alone on a prairie homestead, a woman is handed a rifle by a Mounted Policeman and told to shoot anyone who breaks cover while he searches her farm.

story.title: The Faded Rose
story.blurb: A rich creditor lays a pressed rose before the daughter of the ruined judge and confesses the strange, patient obsession behind every loan he made.
story.spoilerNote: Reveals the creditor's long secret love and his offer of marriage, the early turning point that sets the novel in motion.

story.title: Meeting the Dragon
story.blurb: At a Paris station, a girl with a red rose watches for the ogre she has agreed to meet under a borrowed name. He is nothing like she pictured.

story.title: The Last Lunarians
story.blurb: A ship of explorers sinks into a lightless crater on the moon and finds stagnant water, grey moss, and something that was once, perhaps, human.

story.title: The Make-Believe Bride
story.blurb: Roped into posing for a moving picture crew, a girl and her reluctant guardian play out a runaway wedding at the blacksmith's anvil, and something in the game turns real.
story.spoilerNote: His secret purchase of the wedding gown hints at the romance the book is quietly building toward.
story.brokenNote: The text cuts off mid-sentence in its final line ('because, whatever happens, I'), so the closing thought never lands.

story.title: The Court of Political Justice
story.blurb: A newcomer watches a murder trial where both sides agree the defendant did it, and the only question is what the dead senator did to deserve it.

story.title: Three Puffy Rolls
story.blurb: A soaked, hungry young runaway arrives in a strange city with a dollar in his pocket, buys three great puffy rolls, and walks straight past his future wife's door.

short.title: Arrested for Voting
short.blurb: A deputy marshal rings the doorbell to arrest a woman for the crime of casting a ballot. She insists on being treated like any other criminal.

story.title: The Girl in the Shop Window
story.blurb: A lonely lumberman confides an odd secret: the mannequin in a shop window he passes every noon is breathing, and she is exactly the girl he has dreamed of.

story.title: Bluff on Spaceman's Row
story.blurb: Disguised as a shady freighter crew in a spaceport dive, two undercover lawmen work a scarred stranger for a lead, spinning lies they cannot afford to unravel.

story.title: The Heretic Marriage
story.blurb: An Englishman in Mexico loves a lady the Church refuses to marry to a heretic. He finds his own way to the altar, and the Church does not forgive it.

short.title: The Silence Behind the Door
short.blurb: Alone at midnight, a man lights strange powders, reads from an old book, and waits. The silence that answers is not the silence of an empty room.

21638.pairNote: Separate episodes with different leads; the defiance scene and the tower escape share no text and neither gives away the other's payoff.

short.title: She Would Not Let Him
short.blurb: A conqueror announces a prisoner will die tomorrow. The only thing standing in his way is a girl who calmly tells him no.
short.spoilerNote: Reveals Elza's feelings for the narrator and the conqueror's weakness for her, threads the book develops slowly.

story.title: The Burning Tower
story.blurb: One charge in a borrowed weapon, one princess behind an electrified tower wall, and a city waking to alarms. A rescue with no room to pause.
story.spoilerNote: Shows Wolfgar secretly working for the heroes, an allegiance the book stages as its own discovery.

story.title: The Midnight Search
story.blurb: A jealous old husband storms his young wife's bedroom with lawyers and pistols, hunting a lover. She answers with the most magnificent scolding in Spain.

story.title: The Bear Pit
story.blurb: A pleasant zoo outing turns in an instant when a restless toddler squirms above the sunken bear den, and only one quiet man does not step back.

story.title: The Runaway Scow
story.blurb: A rope snaps and a scow with one crouching passenger is swept into a black-walled canyon; a young man leaps aboard as the rapids ahead begin to roar.

story.title: The Hill at Manassas
story.blurb: Shells scream over a hilltop where a quiet general steadies his men, while up from the smoke below gallops a rider crying that all is lost.

story.title: The Price of a Christian
story.blurb: At a desert well, a traveling Englishman learns that the local chief means to kill him for being a Christian, and the haggling begins.

short.title: Through the Sleeping Camp
short.blurb: A traveler creeps into a strangers' camp at night, watching firelit faces and spinning prayer wheels, then leads his men straight through it in the dark.

short.title: Sold at the Ford
short.blurb: A crowd jeers at a ford as a slave dealer praises his wares: a lean girl with burning eyes, chained wrists, and a welt across her shoulders.

story.title: Firelight and Fury
story.blurb: A young storyteller holds a camp of drovers spellbound with a tale of the afterlife, until one burly listener demands to know how he can know it.

short.title: Not Even a Little Pink
short.blurb: American visitors stand in Red Square and find it, somehow, not red at all; a sour MVD man defends the symbolism of glorious Russia.

short.title: Be You a Real Doctor?
short.blurb: From a miserable makeshift boat, a silent brown-faced figure waits offshore for hours before daring a single question of the doctor at the rail.

short.title: A Reckless Act of Zeal
short.blurb: An English merchant in Portugal, appalled by the worship at a royal wedding, settles his affairs, closes his books, and returns to the cathedral with a New Testament.

story.title: A Card of Lace
story.blurb: A respectable lady buys black lace in a Bath shop; a quarter hour later she stands accused of theft, facing gaol and perhaps transportation.

story.title: A Battleship in the Files
story.blurb: A safecracking agent picks his chief's bedroom lock at midnight to show him proof that someone is quietly building a warship extinct for a thousand years.

story.title: Silver from the Bay of Bengal
story.blurb: By the hot Indian surf, a painter watches a boy ride a log through breakers while a whole village hauls in the glittering catch of the season.

23172.pairNote: The short is the inquest frame and the story is the testimony given there; separate scenes that complement rather than repeat.

short.title: An Incredible Testimony
short.blurb: A dusty young journalist rides hard to reach a mountain cabin inquest, where he must swear under oath to an account he himself calls incredible.

story.title: Something in the Wild Oats
story.blurb: Two hunters cross a quail meadow when the wild oats begin to bend and flatten under something no eye can see, and one of them raises his gun.
story.spoilerNote: It shows the invisible creature's attack that the full story approaches sideways through its inquest frame, though the final explanation is not given.
story.brokenNote: The passage stops mid-sentence in its final line, cutting the climax short.

story.title: Nooses by the Roadside
story.blurb: Bandits swarm a moonlit Roman road and seize two young gentlemen, one wounded, one owing a death, while nooses are already swinging from the trees.

short.title: A Vow in the Moonlight
short.blurb: Hidden beneath a plane tree at night, a man watches a golden haired girl step from a carriage, and she turns as if he had called her name.

23637.pairNote: A parlour dog comedy and a horse race heat; different scenes with different stakes, sharing only one bystander.

short.title: Nerve Enough to Own the World
short.blurb: A brindled intruder strolls in, starts a fight, absorbs a kicking without blinking, and comes away with the household ham and every shred of dignity in the room.

story.title: Saving the Distance
story.blurb: An old preacher and his stiff old pacer face three sleek trotters before a jeering grandstand, needing only to survive the first heat with their distance saved.

story.title: Chichibio and the Crane
story.blurb: A cook gives away one leg of his master's roasted crane and swears cranes have only one, a lie he must prove by the riverside at dawn.

short.title: We Are Friends
short.blurb: A stranded explorer plants himself in the path of a headless barrel creature pushing a cart, holds out both hands, and offers friendship.

short.title: The Forbidden Parlour
short.blurb: A toddler slips at last into the forbidden parlour on a cold morning and finds his mother lying still among flowers, resting for the first time.

story.title: The Ship From Outside
story.blurb: A tiny patrol ship near Pluto meets a stranger half a mile long, and its crew begin dying in perfect silence while two men run for the tender.

24149.pairNote: Separate episodes of the same feud, no shared text and neither steals the other's payoff.

short.title: Gifts With the Morning Milk
short.blurb: A fine meerschaum pipe appears on a detective's doorstep with no card. He knows exactly who sent it, and exactly what he is going to do about it.

story.title: When Your Eyelid Twitches
story.blurb: A detective lists the week's peculiar accidents: burning pants, a scorched getaway driver, a bomb that failed. The calm man across the desk is not curious at all.
story.spoilerNote: It shows Brink knowingly behind the criminals' impossible mishaps, something the full story unfolds more gradually.

story.title: An Audience With the Inquisitor
